title: Deutsche Telekom Bets on AI to Cut Costs, Boost Revenue
key_facts: Deutsche Telekom is targeting EUR 2.5 billion in indirect cost savings, measured against 2023, and EUR 800 million in AI-related enterprise revenue by 2030.
It plans to embed automation across network infrastructure, customer service, software development and enterprise technology.
AI-related business revenue outside the US is expected to reach EUR 250 million in 2026 and EUR 800 million by 2030.
It is building sovereign AI infrastructure, including an Industrial AI Cloud in Munich for industrial simulations and sensitive enterprise workloads.

Its RAN Guardian Agent reportedly cut response times to mobile network congestion from several hours to about one minute; its Frag Magenta chatbot handled 2.6 million customer service calls in the first half of 2026.
In the US, AI agents now manage 40% of customer contacts while overall service call volumes have fallen 55%; more than 100,000 employees have received AI training.
quote_evidence: Deutsche Telekom is betting billions on artificial intelligence to overhaul its operations, targeting €2.5 billion in indirect cost savings and €800 million in AI-related enterprise revenue by 2030.
Its RAN Guardian Agent reportedly reduced response times to emerging mobile network congestion from several hours to approximately one minute.
In the US, AI agents now manage 40% of customer contacts, while overall service call volumes have fallen 55%.
why_it_matters_hint: A large European telecom is putting numbers on how much of its work AI will take over, with questions about jobs and dependence on automated systems.
notes: WSJ article blocked; Intelligent CIO's 9 Oct report covers the same plan and is credited instead. Intelligent CIO does not say where or when the targets were presented, and gives results without independent checking. Not carried in earlier editions.
